 -vs-  The State of West Bengal & Ors.
 Mr. Billwadal Bhattacharyya  Mr. Sabyasachi Chatterjee  Mr. Anish Kumar Mukherjee  Mr. Akashdeep Mukherjee  ... for the petitioners  Mr. Tapan Kumar Mukherjee, Ld. AGP  Mr. Somnath Naskar  ... for the State  Mr. Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya, Sr. Adv.
 Ms. Sayanti Sengupta  Mr. J. Khan  ... for the added respondent Mr. M. Thakur Mr. Swarup Kumar Ghosh ... for respondent nos. 4-5 On January 12, 2021 when this matter was taken up for hearing, we had minuted the following order.

"During the course of hearing today, we thought it appropriate to call upon the District Magistrate of Paschim Medinipur to place on record an appropriate order that may be issued in the exercise of statutory authority and other official powers in consonance with the Disaster Management Act and / or the Criminal Procedure Code, in the wake of the need to appropriately manage matters relating to the 'mela'
in question.
This has to be done particularly keeping in mind the COVID related issues which need to be addressed.
We record the submission of learned counsel for the petitioners that standard operating procedures have been issued by the Government of India.

We see that different notices have been issued from time to time having regard to the types of Dibakar Shee & Ors vs The State Of West Bengal & Ors on 13 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103078196/

sentences.text: We notice that the District Magistrate has in her affidavit sworn on 11.01.2021 stated that the number of COVID cases have come down in the area in question.

All relevant factors will be taken into account and the decision taken in the issue in that regard will be placed before us for consideration when this matter will appear before us, tomorrow, i.e., on 13.01.2021 at 2.00 P.M."
Today learned Additional Government Pleader produces a copy of a memo dated January 12, 2021 issued by the District Magistrate (DM), Paschim Mednipur.
The memo pertains to the COVID-19 protocol that is required to be followed by the organisers of the 'Ghatal Utsab and Sisu Mela'.

The directives contained in the said memo are as follows:
1. Stalls shall be made keeping 20 feet distance from each other.
2. Each venue shall have three gates and shall be manned by sufficient volunteers with sanitizer, mask (to provide mask-less visitors/ participants) and thermal scanners.
3. Satyajit Ray Mukta Mancha and Kushpata Bangabashi Football Ground venues shall be opened only for participants and not for public.
'No entry' board shall be placed at the entry gates for public.

4. No one shall be allowed inside the venue without face mask and must be on their face in position and that has to be ensured through the volunteers.
5.
Entry of pregnant women and aged people above 65 years has to be restricted for their safety.

6. Awareness among the public about COVID-19 protocols and guidelines have to be made continuously and widely through miking in the area and venues on each day of the Mela and flexes at different places in the area, outside and inside of the venues in sufficient numbers and appropriate sizes.
7. The committee shall made (sic: read - make) available doctors at the venues each day for emergency purposes.
8. Ensure each venue sanitized thrice every day - in the morning, at afternoon and at the end.
9.
Ensure not more than ten persons at a time before any stall for buying goods and food and there shall be barricade and circles for standing of visitors/buyers in front of each stall.

sentences.text: Cultural programme shall be restricted to not more than three hours each day.

The memo states that the 'Ghatal Utsab and Sisu Mela' Committee shall organise and hold the 'mela', cultural competitions, sports, etc. following the directions given in the memo and observing COVID-19 protocols in letter and spirit, keeping in mind health of the people above all.

The memo ends by stating that the order has been made in the interest of public service and attracts penal action for wilful neglect, non-observance and non-compliance under the provisions of National Disaster Management Act, 2005.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties with reference to the aforesaid memo.
We are satisfied that if the directives in the aforesaid memo are followed and implemented, there should be no problem in going ahead with the 'mela' and there should be no public health hazard.

We are sure that the people in the administration headed by the District Magistrate, Paschim Medinipur shall ensure that the organisers of the 'mela' scrupulously adhere to the directives contained in the aforesaid memo.

Let this matter be posted on February 5, 2021 when the District Magistrate shall file a report of compliance to the effect that the 'mela' was held adhering to the directives contained in the memo dated 12.01.2021 issued by the District Magistrate, Paschim Medinipur.
The conditions imposed by the said memo shall not be diluted or any exemption granted therefrom.

In response to our query, learned Additional Government Pleader states that though the full name of the signatory to the memo dated 12.01.2021 does not appear thereon, but it has been signed by Dr. Rashmi Kamal, District Magistrate of Paschim Medinipur.
The petitioners apprise us by showing photographs that stalls have been set up without keeping 20 feet distance as is required by the memo issued by the District Magistrate.
We are sure that the stalls will be operated strictly in terms of the conditions mentioned in the aforesaid memo.
(Thottathil B. Radhakrishnan, CJ.)

(Arijit Banerjee, J.)
